blind_spots.blind_spot: The company brags about 'improved SWaP-C relative to the competition' in general SDR marketing, but for the specific Navy fiber-laser sensor SBIR, nothing addresses shipboard integration reality — power draw from ship's electrical systems, EMI shielding, or how a fiber-optic acoustic sensor array survives years of shipboard vibration and salt-air exposure between drydock cycles.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Naval platforms run multi-year duty cycles in salt-air, high-vibration, EMI-dense environments; a sensor system optimized for SWaP-C on a bench doesn't automatically survive that without a stated corrosion/vibration-hardening and sustainment plan.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The public site markets general custom-engineering capability, not the specific fielded-platform requirements of the one named defense product line.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our SDR solutions perform signal processing, acquisition, and waveform synthesis with higher throughput, wider bandwidth, greater parallelization, and improved SWaP-C relative to the competition.

blind_spots.blind_spot: The company frames itself entirely as a contract engineering shop ('You Dream It. We Build It.') building to whatever spec clients bring, with the Navy fiber-laser sensor system appearing only inside an SBIR abstract rather than as a flagship product with its own page, CONOPS, or Navy sponsor named publicly.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Without a visible champion above the program-office level for this specific sensor system, the classic SBIR failure mode applies: technically sound Phase II engineering with no publicly evident path to a Phase III fielding decision.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: As a small custom-engineering shop, the company's public identity is built around general capability-for-hire, not around advocating any single program to a fielded outcome.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The Sky is No Longer the Limit. You Dream It. We Build It.

blind_spots.blind_spot: A second, brand-new Navy SBIR Phase I (Dec 2025) is now running in parallel with the 2022 Phase II fiber-laser sensor program on the same ~10-person team, with no public discussion of how the team splits engineering hours across two funded defense R&D efforts plus ongoing custom client work.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A 10-person shop juggling a Phase II sensor program, a brand-new Phase I, and paying custom-engineering work is exactly the resource-constrained situation where the funded-months-remaining clock outruns actual available engineering bandwidth.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The two SBIR awards were announced three years apart as separate wins; nothing in the company's materials connects them into a single resourcing picture.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Sequent Logic, LLC has received a $139,998 award from the Department of Defense, Department of the Navy, as part of the Small Business Innovation Research Program Phase I.

opener_hook: You're running a Navy Phase II fiber-laser sensor program and a brand-new Navy Phase I at the same time on a 10-person team — which one gets the engineering hours this quarter?
